title: Check yourself: Independent passes, combined verdicts and the practice

questions.stem: Scenario S2, code generation with Claude Code. A team reviews each change in a separate run, yet nearly every verdict is still approval, because the run is also handed the author's rationale for each change. Which step removes the remaining cause?

options.text: Keep the notes and add a second review turn in the same conversation
options.says: Ruled out because the option is "a second review in the same conversation, which adds a third reader who shares the first two readers' context".

options.text: Drop the notes and give the new instance the diff and the criteria
options.says: The page says "the reasoning that justified the code is still in the context", and the notes carry that reasoning into the new instance, so withholding them removes the cause.

options.text: Keep the notes and raise the thinking budget until verdicts stop approving
options.says: Ruled out because it is "a larger thinking budget, which gives the model more room to reason from the same starting point".

options.text: Keep the notes and ask the instance to write a stricter checklist first
options.says: Ruled out because a checklist is "a stricter instruction in the same conversation, since the reasoning is still there".

questions.stem: Scenario S6, structured data extraction. A verification pass gives each extracted claim a confidence score, and claims scored 95 or more are accepted without further checks. An audit finds wrong claims among the accepted ones. Which change fits best?

options.text: Accept at 99 instead, because a higher bar lets fewer wrong ones through
options.says: Ruled out because "a number the same pass produced about its own finding carries the same blind spot as the finding".

options.text: Have the same pass explain its score and accept when the explanation reads sound
options.says: Ruled out because "confident-but-wrong claim is confident because the reasoning behind it looked sound to its author", so a sound-sounding explanation proves nothing.

options.text: Send the lowest-scoring tenth to a person and accept the rest as they are
options.says: Ruled out because "a finding reported by one pass is not accepted on confidence alone, however high", and this option accepts the rest on exactly that.

options.text: Have a separate instance try to refute each one before it is trusted
options.says: A score the same pass produced about its own claim is not independent evidence, and another instance that tries to refute the claim is.

origin.section: Confidence that does not verify itself
